mainEntity.name: How long does dental bonding typically maintain its original appearance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental bonding typically maintains its best appearance for 3-7 years, depending on location, oral habits, and care. Front teeth bonding may show changes sooner due to higher visibility of subtle alterations, whilst back teeth bonding often maintains function longer but may experience more wear from chewing forces.

mainEntity.name: Can professional teeth whitening improve the appearance of dull bonded teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Professional teeth whitening treatments do not affect composite bonding materials, which means bonded areas will not lighten along with natural teeth. If whitening is desired, the natural teeth are typically whitened first, and then bonding may need replacement to match the new shade of the natural teeth.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for bonded teeth to feel rougher over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some surface texture changes are normal as composite materials age, but significant roughness may indicate excessive wear or surface deterioration. Professional assessment can determine whether polishing or other treatment would improve both comfort and appearance of the bonded area.

mainEntity.name: What causes some bonded teeth to look more obvious than others?

acceptedAnswer.text: The visibility of bonded teeth depends on factors including the skill of placement, colour matching accuracy, surface finishing, and the location of the bonding. Bonding on front teeth requires more precise colour matching and surface finishing to blend naturally with surrounding teeth.

mainEntity.name: Can I prevent my bonded teeth from becoming dull?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whilst some changes are inevitable over time, good oral hygiene, limiting exposure to staining substances, avoiding excessive force or grinding, and regular professional care can significantly slow the development of dullness in bonded teeth.

mainEntity.name: Should I be concerned if my bonded teeth look different from my natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some difference in appearance between bonded and natural teeth is normal due to material properties. However, rapid changes, significant colour differences, or surface irregularities warrant professional assessment to ensure the bonding remains in good condition and determine if any treatment would be beneficial.
